profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This dude keeps giving you the weirdest possible golf: plenty of looks from the fairway, enough greens to stay annoying, then a putting line that keeps the blood pressure up. The ball isn’t traveling like some launch-monitor hero, but the tee shot is usually functional enough to keep the round from detonating. What makes the file interesting is the swing between clean-ish ball control and the occasional full grease fire around the scoring holes. It’s not pretty, but it keeps showing up near the top because the mess is controlled, not cured.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file that makes you squint at the scorecard and wonder how the hell it still kind of works. The tee ball has been the recurring crime scene: not much help, not much forgiveness, and too often the rest of the bag gets dragged into the alley with it. There are enough flashes with the putter to keep him from fully face-planting, but the approach game keeps spraying receipts all over the place. It’s a volatile build — some rounds survive on damage control, others just keep bleeding bogeys until the cart girl files a complaint.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: BOGEY MACHINE, OCCASIONAL BIRDIE TAX REFUND
profiles.profile: This profile reads like a guy who can’t quite decide whether he’s built to score or built to survive. The tee ball is usually respectable, the ball in play is often good enough, and then the rest of the round gets mugged by misses that turn into ugly doubles and a lot of unnecessary stress. When the putter shows up, he can fake competence; when it doesn’t, the card gets loud fast. There’s enough structure here to keep him around, but the scoring system still gets fed a steady diet of self-inflicted nonsense.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: BOMB IT, THEN START THE FIRE
profiles.profile: This dude lives in the high-speed end of the range and then immediately starts negotiating with the consequences. The driver has real juice, but the accuracy is so flaky that it often feels like the ball is filing a missing-person report off the tee. Weirdly, the short game and putter have been capable of rescuing enough messes to keep him dangerous, which is why the file never fully collapses into chaos. When the irons are even halfway on, he can look nasty; when they aren’t, it turns into a very expensive math problem.
